title: Outlook: grant mailbox and folder delegate permissions from the new Outlook
summary: Hold: Microsoft Support documents folder and mailbox sharing permission levels in both new Outlook and Outlook on the web, which the briefing treats as unpublished. The existing Exchange controls and licensing statements check out, but the briefing needs to distinguish the stale roadmap status from the functionality Microsoft already documents.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans to let users grant mailbox and folder delegate access from new Outlook.
claims.quote: Delegate access for mailbox and folders can be granted from the new Outlook app.

claims.claim: The roadmap says users will be able to view permissions granted for mailboxes and folders.
claims.quote: Users will be able to view the permissions granted for a mailboxes and folders.

claims.quote: #newoutlookforwindows

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page describes this specific roadmap feature yet.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook grant delegate mailbox folder permissions 417063; "new Outlook" "delegate" "permissions" "sharing" 417063. Opened cited Learn pages and Microsoft's Support sharing and delegate articles; found Support instructions, not a Learn feature page.
claims.fix: Replace the documentation-gap wording with: 'Microsoft Support documents mailbox and folder sharing in new Outlook, while the supplied roadmap record still lists In development with a July CY2026 target.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/office/share-and-access-another-person-s-mailbox-or-folder-in-outlook-a909ad30-e413-40b5-a487-0ea70b763081. Do not describe the roadmap as the only source about the functionality.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said which permission types the new Outlook sharing screens grant, including folder roles.
claims.quote: In the Permissions section, select the Permission level dropdown and select the permissions you want to grant to this user.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket gap with: 'Microsoft Support documents folder permission levels in new Outlook, including Owner, Publishing Editor, Editor, Publishing Author, Author, Nonediting Author, Reviewer, Contributor, None and Custom. This does not establish that the screens grant Exchange Full Access or Send as.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/office/share-and-access-another-person-s-mailbox-or-folder-in-outlook-a909ad30-e413-40b5-a487-0ea70b763081 and narrow the repeated open question to the remaining mailbox-level permissions.

claims.where: What's changing; controls notes; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly identify these roadmap screens as the implementation of the cited Exchange administrative operations.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" "grant" "delegate access" "permissions"; 417063 delegate permissions. Read Exchange recipient/calendar permissions, Add-MailboxFolderPermission, and Support sharing instructions; none explicitly maps this roadmap item's screens to those administrative operations.

claims.claim: Users assigned Full Access, Send as or Send on behalf on another mailbox are called delegates.
claims.quote: The users that are assigned these permissions on other mailboxes or groups are called delegates.

claims.claim: An Outlook calendar delegate has the Editor calendar role.
claims.quote: An Outlook delegate has the Editor calendar role and a Delegate sharing permission flag.

claims.claim: An Outlook calendar delegate has the Delegate sharing permission flag.
claims.quote: An Outlook delegate has the Editor calendar role and a Delegate sharing permission flag.

claims.claim: Learn says to configure delegate relationships from Outlook while the calendar owner is signed in.
claims.quote: Configure delegate relationships from Outlook while the calendar owner is signed in.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Full Access permits opening a mailbox and viewing, adding and removing its contents.
claims.quote: Allows the delegate to open the mailbox, and view, add and remove the contents of the mailbox.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Send as makes a message appear to come directly from the mailbox without indicating the delegate.
claims.quote: Allows the delegate to send messages as if they came directly from the mailbox or group. There's no indication that the message was sent by the delegate.

claims.claim: Send on behalf identifies the delegate in the From address.
claims.quote: The From address of these messages clearly shows that the message was sent by the delegate

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Full Access delegates can read IRM-protected messages in a user mailbox by default.
claims.quote: By default, for a user mailbox, Information Rights Management (IRM)-protected email messages can be read by any delegate who has Full Access permission on the mailbox.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn describes different methods for preventing IRM delegate access according to the client and scenario.
claims.quote: Use the following table to determine the appropriate prevention method for each scenario.

claims.claim: Calendar delegate access does not include viewing private items by default; CanViewPrivateItems grants that ability.
claims.quote: CanViewPrivateItems lets the user view private calendar items. Delegate access doesn't include this capability by default.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified whether the roadmap item's new screens expose the private-calendar-item flag.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" "delegate" "permissions" "sharing" 417063; "new Outlook" "grant" "delegate access" "permissions". Read calendar delegate permissions and Support mailbox/folder sharing and delegate overview; no private-item flag for this item's screens was specified.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Folder sharing requires access on the shared folder and its parent folders, and partial grants can prevent opening it.
claims.quote: the user has to grant the other person access to the specific folder that the user wants to share and also to all other parent folders in the folder hierarchy.
claims.fix: Qualify the existing guidance with: 'Microsoft Support says new Outlook and Outlook on the web preserve existing parent-folder permissions and automatically assign Folder visible where parent folders have no permissions assigned.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/office/share-and-access-another-person-s-mailbox-or-folder-in-outlook-a909ad30-e413-40b5-a487-0ea70b763081 so readers are not told that these clients always require manual parent-folder grants.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The cited troubleshooting article requires at least Folder visible for the default role on the root Mailbox folder.
claims.quote: The root folder (the Mailbox folder) in Outlook must be assigned at least Folder visible permissions for the default role.

claims.claim: Insufficient mailbox-folder access can produce the stated Unable to open default folders error.
claims.quote:
Unable to open default folders-you do not have permissions to logon

This issue occurs if the user doesn't have sufficient permissions to access the mailbox folder.

claims.claim: The roadmap description specifies user grants and permission viewing, not an agent or automated action.
claims.quote: Delegate access for mailbox and folders can be granted from the new Outlook app. Users will be able to view the permissions granted for a mailboxes and folders.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Delegation gives another person access, and their permitted actions depend on the granted permissions.
claims.quote: you can use the Exchange admin center (EAC) or Exchange Online PowerShell to assign permissions to a mailbox or group so that other users can access the mailbox

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The EAC Mailbox delegation view can be used to inventory mailbox-level delegates.
claims.quote: In the properties of the mailbox in the EAC, verify the delegate is or isn't listed in Mailbox delegation > Full Access.

claims.claim: Using Outlook for Windows with a Microsoft 365 organisational account requires a desktop-app plan, with Business Standard and Business Premium as examples.
claims.quote: For example, a Business Standard or Business Premium plan provides access to a Microsoft 365 email address and the desktop versions of Outlook and other Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included in the product licence rather than an independently identified feature add-on.
claims.quote: To use the Outlook for Windows desktop app (either the classic or new version) with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address, you need to purchase a plan that includes the desktop versions of the Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.claim: After adding an account with a qualifying desktop licence, secondary Business Basic or E1 accounts can be added.
claims.quote: Once you add an account with a qualifying license to Outlook, you can add secondary accounts with licenses for products that don't include the desktop apps such as Business Basic or E1.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence or meter specific to this roadmap item has been published beyond the product's general licensing requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" "delegation" license pricing meter; new Outlook grant delegate mailbox folder permissions 417063 default licensing admin disable. Read Outlook licensing, Exchange recipient permissions and Support sharing prerequisites; no item-specific add-on or meter was stated.

claims.claim: The Exchange recipient-permissions article does not list a licence prerequisite for assigning the three mailbox permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" "delegation" license pricing meter. Read Manage permissions for recipients in Exchange Online in full, including What do you need to know before you begin; it specifies assigned permissions, not a licence prerequisite.

claims.claim: The roadmap record does not specify licence requirements or configuration roles, or identify particular user cohorts.
claims.quote: Delegate access for mailbox and folders can be granted from the new Outlook app. Users will be able to view the permissions granted for a mailboxes and folders. #newoutlookforwindows

claims.claim: Administrators need assigned permissions to perform the existing Exchange recipient-permission procedures.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can perform this procedure or procedures.

claims.claim: The Exchange article points to the Mailbox settings entry in Feature permissions in Exchange Online for required permissions.
claims.quote: To see what permissions you need, see the "Mailbox settings" entry in the Feature permissions in Exchange Online article.

claims.claim: Exchange permission support differs by recipient type, including user, shared and resource mailboxes.
claims.quote: Send on behalf: Messages sent by a delegate have "<Delegate> on behalf of <Mailbox>" in the From address. Note that this permission isn't available in the EAC for shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy restrictions on folder-permission changes cover new Outlook.
claims.quote: Restrict users from changing folder permissions in classic Outlook, new Outlook, and Outlook on the Web

claims.claim: Turn off sharing recommendation is one of the policies Microsoft says to enable for the folder restriction.
claims.quote: Enable each of the following policies: Turn off sharing recommendation

claims.claim: Do not allow users to change permissions on folders is one of the required policies.
claims.quote: Do not allow users to change permissions on folders

claims.claim: Control Calendar Sharing is one of the required policies.
claims.quote: Control Calendar Sharing

claims.claim: These policies are configured in a policy configuration under Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. To view a list of policy configurations, select Customization > Policy Management. Create a new policy configuration, and select the applicable scope.

claims.claim: A separate switch specifically covering all of this roadmap item's new screens is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" delegate permissions default enable disable OwaMailboxPolicy; "DelegateAccessEnabled" "new Outlook". Read folder restrictions, Outlook access-policy search excerpts and Set-OwaMailboxPolicy's DelegateAccessEnabled excerpt; none states a switch's reach over all item 417063 screens.

claims.claim: The printed EAC path reaches Add members for Read and manage (Full Access).
claims.quote: Click Mailbox Delegation and configure one or more of the following permissions: ... Read and manage (Full Access) ... To assign permissions to delegates, click Edit under the appropriate permission, and then click ... Add members.

claims.claim: The printed Add-MailboxPermission call grants FullAccess with the documented target, user and inheritance parameters.
claims.quote: Add-MailboxPermission -Identity <MailboxIdentity> -User <DelegateIdentity> -AccessRights FullAccess -InheritanceType All [-AutoMapping $false]

claims.claim: The printed classic Outlook folder Properties > Permissions path adds a user and reaches Permission Level.
claims.quote: Right-click the folder that you want to move, and then select Properties. ... On the Permissions tab, if you aren't listed, add your name. ... Select your name, and then select Owner for the Permission Level.

claims.claim: Add-MailboxFolderPermission accepts the printed mailbox-folder identity, User and AccessRights role parameters to add folder permissions.
claims.quote:
Add-MailboxFolderPermission -Identity ayla@contoso.com:\Marketing -User ed@contoso.com -AccessRights Owner

This example grants the Owner role to Ed on the Marketing folder in Ayla's mailbox.

claims.claim: SharingPermissionFlags Delegate applies to calendar folders in the cmdlet examples.
claims.quote: The SharingPermissionFlags parameter assigns calendar delegate permissions. This parameter only applies to calendar folders and can only be used when the AccessRights parameter value is Editor.

claims.claim: Add-RecipientPermission is used to grant Send as.
claims.quote: You use the Add-RecipientPermission and Remove-RecipientPermission cmdlets to manage the Send As permission for mailboxes and groups.

claims.claim: Set-Mailbox uses GrantSendOnBehalfTo to manage Send on behalf.
claims.quote: Set-Mailbox -Identity seanc@contoso.com -GrantSendOnBehalfTo hollyh

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell is appropriate for calendar-folder permission administration but not preferred for creating a complete delegate relationship.
claims.quote: Exchange Online PowerShell is appropriate for calendar folder permission administration and validation, but it isn't the preferred method for creating a complete delegate relationship.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether both new Outlook for Windows and the web client have the mailbox/folder sharing screens.
claims.quote: Share and access a folder or mailbox in new Outlook ... Share and access a folder or mailbox in Outlook on the web
claims.fix: Replace the platform uncertainty with: 'The roadmap record lists Web and carries #newoutlookforwindows. Microsoft Support documents Sharing and permissions for mailbox and folder sharing in both new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web, although the supplied roadmap record remains In development.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/office/share-and-access-another-person-s-mailbox-or-folder-in-outlook-a909ad30-e413-40b5-a487-0ea70b763081. Remove the repeated question about whether these two clients have sharing screens; retain the separate question about shared and resource mailbox coverage.
